title: Leaving Notion
summary: Get documents, wikis and databases out of Notion and into tools you control, without pretending that databases survive the trip.
audience: One person or a small team with a Notion workspace made of documents, a wiki and a handful of databases.
timeframe: One to three weeks. Exporting takes minutes; deciding what each database should become takes the time.

stack.why: The smoothest import for document-heavy workspaces, with real-time editing and permissions. It is source-available rather than open source.
Keeps the database-and-pages way of working. Free for one person; teams pay per seat, self-hosted or not.
For individuals who want local notes with backlinks and no server at all.

phases.title: Take stock
phases.intro: Most workspaces are a few dozen pages that matter and several hundred that do not.

steps.title: Sort your content into three piles
steps.detail: Documents and wiki pages; databases that are really just lists; and databases that run a process, with relations, formulas or automations. The first two migrate well. The third pile needs a decision for each database.

steps.title: List public pages, forms and embeds
steps.detail: Anything published to the web, shared with guests, or embedded in another site will break. Write down each URL and who depends on it.

steps.title: List integrations and automations
steps.detail: Connected apps, API scripts, buttons and database automations. Note what each one does so that you can rebuild or retire it.

steps.title: Delete what you would never look for
steps.detail: Empty pages, abandoned drafts, templates you never used. Everything you delete now is something you do not have to check after the import.

steps.title: Choose where each pile goes
steps.detail: One destination is simplest, but not required. A common split: documents to a wiki, simple lists to spreadsheets or the wiki's tables, and process databases to a dedicated tool or a rebuilt AppFlowy database.

steps.title: Set up the new tool
steps.detail: Install it or open a hosted account. For Outline, self-hosting needs a sign-in provider before anyone can log in, so sort that out first. For Logseq and solo AppFlowy there is nothing to host.

steps.title: Sketch the top-level structure
steps.detail: Decide the handful of top-level collections or spaces before importing. An import that mirrors years of accidental Notion nesting gives you the same mess in a new place.

steps.title: Import one section as a trial
steps.detail: Export a single teamspace or page tree from Notion and import it. Look at nested pages, images, tables, code blocks and links between pages. Adjust your plan according to what you see.

steps.title: Export the whole workspace, twice
steps.detail: Once as Markdown & CSV for importing, and once as HTML as a faithful archive that you can open in any browser years from now. Include subpages and files in both.

steps.title: Import documents and wiki pages
steps.detail: Run the importer on the Markdown export, section by section if the tool allows. Check the page count against Notion's.

steps.title: Rebuild the databases that matter
steps.detail: Import each CSV as a table or grid, then recreate by hand the relations, formulas and views that people actually use. Leave purely historical databases as CSV files in the archive.

steps.title: Repair links between pages
steps.detail: Search the imported content for links that still point to notion.so or notion.com and repoint them. Internal links are the most common casualty of any wiki migration.

steps.title: Set permissions again
steps.detail: Notion's sharing settings do not export. Apply access rules to collections in the new tool, starting with anything confidential, before you invite the team.

steps.title: Make Notion read-only
steps.detail: Change members to read-only access where your plan allows, and put a banner at the top of the main pages with the new address. Anything edited in Notion after the export is lost otherwise.

steps.title: Republish public pages
steps.detail: Publish replacements for the public pages on your list and update the links that point to them from your website, email signatures and other tools.

steps.title: Update links in other tools
steps.detail: Chat channel topics, issue templates, onboarding documents and browser bookmarks all point at Notion. Fix the shared ones and tell people to fix their own.

steps.title: Store the archive in two places
steps.detail: Keep both exports somewhere that is backed up and independent of the new tool. Open the HTML archive once to check that it works offline.

steps.title: Keep Notion for a month and note what people go back for
steps.detail: Every return visit is a page that was missed or a database that was not rebuilt. Fix those, then stop.

steps.title: Downgrade, then delete the workspace
steps.detail: Move to the free plan at the end of the billing period. When a month has passed without anyone needing it, delete the workspace.
